# M0 measures: the sound source (R0)

No cue was built for shipping this round: `assets/audio/**` and `src/audio/manifest.ts` are as committed. Nobody has listened to any of this.

## Banks

| Letter | Bank | File | MB | Licence name |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | TimGM6mb (apt `timgm6mb-soundfont` 1.3-5) | `TimGM6mb.sf2` | 5.97 | GPL-2 |
| B | Fluid (R3) GM (apt `fluid-soundfont-gm` 3.1-5.3) | `FluidR3_GM.sf2` | 148.40 | MIT |
| C | MuseScore General (apt `musescore-general-soundfont` 0.2.1-1) | `MuseScore_General_Full.sf3` | 85.97 | MIT, parts PD or CC0 |
| D | GeneralUser GS v2.0.3 (GitHub `mrbumpy409/GeneralUser-GS`, `main`) | `GeneralUser-GS.sf2` | 32.32 | GeneralUser GS License v2.0 |

All four load and render in `spessasynth_core` 4.4.2. C needed one fix in `render.mjs`: the SF3 (Ogg Vorbis) decoder must be awaited before the bank is read. Sha256, licence quotations and where each licence was read are in `tools/audio/BANKS.md`. D's licence file also states that the author cannot be 100% sure where all contained samples originated.

## Stem audit (bank A, today's charts)

`python3 audit.py downtown suburbs industrial`. Lead tracks come from the `leads=` each chart passes to `lofi_finish`. Each stem is rendered alone, folded and mastered as the build masters a loop (`post.lofi_loop`), not normalised. Integrated loudness is gated, so a lead that is silent for part of the loop is measured over the bars where it plays; the bed plays throughout.

| Loop | Lead tracks | Lead LUFS | Bed LUFS | Lead minus bed (LU) | Same, raw render before mastering |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| downtown | accordion, pizzicato | -40.4 | -35.2 | -5.2 | -4.8 |
| suburbs | muted trumpet, glockenspiel | -42.6 | -35.9 | -6.7 | -6.0 |
| industrial | tenor sax | -37.8 | -36.6 | -1.2 | -0.4 |

Result: the plan's guess that the leads sit 2-3 dB above the bed is not what these three loops measure. Each lead track sits at or below the rest of its loop (-1.2 to -6.7 LU), so all three already meet the "0 LU or less" rule. The measure is gated loudness of each stem rendered alone; it says nothing about spectral prominence or masking.

## Timbre table

These numbers are a proxy for harshness and droning, not an audition: nobody has listened. Phrase: city motif opening (scale degrees 1 3 5 6 5, C major from C4, velocity 64, 80 bpm). Held note: C4, 2 s, velocity 64. Centroid and 2-5 kHz share are from the phrase; sustain ratio is RMS from 1.0 to 1.5 s over RMS of the first 0.2 s of the held note. The warm pad has a slow attack, so its ratio above 1 reflects the swell, not a drone. Every bank has its own preset for every program listed (no fallbacks).

## Reels

`python3 reel.py R0` gives `build/reel/R0.mp3` (62.8 s, stereo, 128 kbps, -16.0 LUFS, peak -3.6 dBFS, one static gain of +3.7 dB) and `R0.txt`. Clips are 12 s from the first bar line after the accordion's first note (the accordion enters on a one-beat pickup into bar 4, so the clip starts at bar 4, 7.27 s into the loop). Each clip comes from a whole loop mastered at -20 LUFS, then cut. Clip 1 is today's Downtown through A; clips 2-5 are the sketch (accordion track as nylon guitar, 0.7 x velocity, via `sketch_r0.py`) through A, B, C, D. `python3 reel.py R1` gives `R1.mp3` (244.9 s, the first 30 s of each shipped music file, -16.0 LUFS, peak -1.3 dBFS, static gain +4.4 dB).

## Build time

One full `python3 build.py` with bank A took 128 s (2.1 minutes), including the sound effects. `build.py downtown` with no `BANK` file passes and writes `build/bank.json` naming TimGM6mb; `tools/audio/BANK` does not exist yet, so every build still renders through A.
